name: DomeGallery-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The sphere is centred and largest, with the tile grid, edge fade and curvature all clearly readable.

tagline: A hollow sphere of small photos you can spin around.
summary: Dozens of rounded photo tiles wrap around a virtual sphere that fills the view. Dragging turns the ball of images with momentum, and clicking one tile enlarges it toward the middle.
appearance: Many small rounded-square photos, all greyscale, sit in a curved grid over a black stage, forming the front of a large sphere. The outer edges fade into darkness while the centre stays sharp and dense.
behaviour: Dragging spins the sphere sideways, with only a small vertical tilt allowed, and momentum carries it after release. Clicking a tile expands that photo toward the centre over a dimmed backdrop.
demo_content: Twelve Unsplash portraits and lifestyle photos, repeated across the sphere and shown in grayscale.
search_phrases: immersive photo wall in the round
drag to spin a ball of pictures
grayscale photo globe for a landing page
click a tile to enlarge it
use_when: A portfolio or campaign wants an immersive, browsable wall of images instead of a flat grid.
avoid_when: It needs a sized parent and many image downloads, and the drag is pointer-only.
customise: Images, fit basis, radius bounds, segment count, grayscale, blur colour, drag feel and the opened image size and radius are props.
weight_why: A 3D sphere of about two hundred image tiles that all re-transform together while it spins.

a11y.note: Tiles are labelled buttons and Escape closes the viewer, but Enter or Space never opens a tile and no focus ring is drawn.

issues: All photos are forced to greyscale by default, which hides the colour of the imagery.
Only a fixed number of tile slots exist, so a larger image set is partly dropped with a console warning.
polish_why: Immersive and coherent with a smooth edge fade, though the grey wash flattens every photo.
title: DomeGallery
